title: test-0081-GEN-ANAEMIA
passage: Today in our science lab, we explored why our blood is red and how our bodies stay energetic. We learned that haemoglobin, a protein in our red blood cells, acts like a tiny transport vehicle that carries oxygen to every part of our body. This oxygen is what our cells use to produce the energy we need to run and play. We also discussed anaemia, a condition where the body lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen efficiently. It is not a contagious disease that spreads by touch, nor does it mean a person has a low total volume of blood. Instead, it often happens when we do not get enough iron or other nutrients. Interestingly, not all iron in our food is absorbed equally; for instance, drinking tea with meals can block iron absorption, even if the tea is weak. While iron-folic acid tablets are often given in school programmes to prevent anaemia, they are not a replacement for a balanced diet. Eating iron-rich foods like spinach and lentils remains essential for everyone, not just those who feel tired or pale. Maintaining healthy iron levels is a daily habit, not just a quick fix for when we feel unwell.
summary: We learned that a protein in our red blood cells carries oxygen to our body. We also discussed anaemia, a condition where the body lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen efficiently.
